# Configuring Entra ID (previously known as Azure AD) single sign-on

### 1. Obtain the metadata file in Securiti

1. In the main menu, from the upper left corner of the left navigation bar, click the **Jewel** icon.
2. From the Platform Services section in the navigation bar, select **Settings**.
3. On the **System Settings** menu, choose **Organizational > Access Management > Service Provider**.
4. On the **Service provider** page, on the top right side of the page, click **Edit**.
5. In the **Configuration Information** section, copy and save the **SP Metadata** and **ACS Url** values for later use.
6. (Optional) In SSL Certificate Setup:
  1. To upload your custom SSL private key and certificate, and mark **Use custom SSL certificate and key**. It shows you the following options:
    - Upload Private Key
    - Upload Certificate
  2. To enforce the SSL verification on connection to the IdP for Post Binding:
    1. Mark **Enforce SSL Verification**.
    2. From the **Algorithm** dropdown menu, select a preferred algorithm for encryption.
    3. On the Service Provider page, record the following information to use later:
      - SP Metadata
      - ACS URL
  3. Once done, on the top right of the page, click **Save Changes.**

![](data:image/png;base64,)

### 2. Configure single sign-on in Entra ID (previously known as Azure)

1. Login to the Azure console with your admin credentials and navigate to **Azure Active Directory**.
2. On the left side menu, click **Enterprise Applications**, then click **New Application**.
3. Click Create your own application.
4. On the Create your own application popup, for the name enter **Securiti** and choose **Integrate any other application**, then click **Create**.
5. On the page for the new Securiti application you created, click **Set up single sign on**, then click **SAML**.
6. On SAML Setup page for the Securiti application, click Upload metadata file, and navigate to the SP metadata file you downloaded in [1. Obtain the metadata file in Securiti](/v1/docs/configuring-entra-id-previously-known-as-azure-ad-single-sign-on).
7. In the User Attributes & Claims area, click **Edit**, then click **Add claim**.
8. On the Add New Claim page, apply the following settings, click **Save** after you enter each name/attribute pair:

| Name | Source Attribute |
| --- | --- |
| email | user.mail |
| first_name | user.givenname |
| last_name | user.surname |

> [!NOTE]
> **Important**
> 
> The claim name for each name/attribute pair must **not** have any prefix as in the following xml: `&lt;Attribute Name=“http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/email”&gt;`. Make sure that your IDP is not adding anything to the claim.
9. After adding all three claims, Go back to the SAML configuration page for the Securiti app.
10. In the User Attributes & Claims area, confirm the new claims for email, first_name, and last_name as shown below.

![AzureAD_user_attribute___claims.png](https://cdn.us.document360.io/37f15d15-eeac-4caf-9724-25918cca6992/Images/Documentation/uuid-62756938-4ff7-3ff1-b0ac-7c1c9b0f6560(3).png)
11. From the SAML configuration page, record the App Federation Metadata URL as shown below to use later.

![SAML_Signing_Certificate.png](https://cdn.us.document360.io/37f15d15-eeac-4caf-9724-25918cca6992/Images/Documentation/uuid-967e76b5-7703-2bfe-e72e-942f6c38fd9b(3).png)

### 3. Configuring user role and organization in Azure for new users (Optional)

You can configure the user role and organization in Azure. Securiti then assigns these roles to the users every time the user logs in to Securiti using Azure.

1. On the Microsoft Azure console, go to the **Enterprise Applications** and go to **App Registration** from the left sidebar. Choose the application created in the **Configure single sign-on in Entra ID (previously known as Azure)** section.

![app-registrations.png](https://cdn.us.document360.io/37f15d15-eeac-4caf-9724-25918cca6992/Images/Documentation/uuid-6c4a2aa9-e4d4-e4cd-104b-66bb40906ddd(3).png)
2. Open the selected application, then navigate to **App Roles** from the left-side menu.

![app-roles.png](https://cdn.us.document360.io/37f15d15-eeac-4caf-9724-25918cca6992/Images/Documentation/uuid-ceb79799-1c23-18b0-e3db-95f86337f0e8(3).png)
3. Click on the **Create app role** button. Add **Display name** as per the requirement, for example, *UserRole*, and enter the **Value**.

> [!NOTE]
> **Important**
> 
> For any role names with spaces, pass the role names without spaces in the value, for example, *OrganizationAdmin*. All roles are supported except **User** and **Module Owner**.

The list of roles is given below.

| Role title | Role to use in Azure |
| --- | --- |
| DPO | DPO |
| Operator | Operator |
| Organization Admin | OrganizationAdmin |
| Super Admin | SuperAdmin |
| Assessment Module Owner Role | AssessmentModuleOwnerRole |
| Assessment User Role | AssessmentUserRole |
| Data Breach Module Owner Role | DataBreachModuleOwnerRole |
| Datamap Module Owner Role | DatamapModuleOwnerRole |
| Datamap user Role | DatamapuserRole |
| DSR Module Owner Role | DSRModuleOwnerRole |
| DSR User Role | DSRUserRole |
| SSP Module Owner Role | SSPModuleOwnerRole |
| SSP User Role | SSPUserRole |
| Vendor Assessment Module Owner Role | VendorAssessmentModuleOwnerRole |
| Vendor Assessment User Role | VendorAssessmentUserRole |

Add the description in the textbox as required. Click on **Apply** to apply the changes.

![create-app-role.png](https://cdn.us.document360.io/37f15d15-eeac-4caf-9724-25918cca6992/Images/Documentation/uuid-863c128b-3fe9-f09d-d2a8-06f754ed3f26(3).png)
4. The next step is to add the attributes for role name and organization in the Attributes and Claims. navigate to the application and go to the **Single sign on** setting. Click on **Set up single sign on**.

![setup-single-sign-on.png](https://cdn.us.document360.io/37f15d15-eeac-4caf-9724-25918cca6992/Images/Documentation/uuid-060ca895-a540-9006-cf4e-84642086be88(3).png)
5. In the Attributes and Claims section, click **Edit** to edit the user attributes and claims.
6. On the **Attributes and Claims** page, click on the **Add new claim** button.
  1. To add the **role name**, add the claim with any of the following options against the **Name** and select the **Source** as **Attribute**:

In the **Source attribute** column select `user.assignedroles` from the dropdown menu.
    1. `securiti_role_azure`
    2. `role_azure`
    3. `securitiroleazure`
    4. `roleazure`
  2. To add **organization**, add `org_name` against the **Name** and select the **Source** as **Attribute**. In the Source attribute column select *user.companyname* from the dropdown menu.

![org-name-claims.png](https://cdn.us.document360.io/37f15d15-eeac-4caf-9724-25918cca6992/Images/Documentation/uuid-badfe480-5c44-7f34-7d34-a6ae18850109(3).png)

To add multiple organizations based on group membership, you must add commas between multiple organization names.

![](https://cdn.us.document360.io/37f15d15-eeac-4caf-9724-25918cca6992/Images/Documentation/AddMultipleOrganizations(1).png)
7. You can go back to the **Attributes and Claims** page to verify that the role and organization name attribute is successfully added under the **Additional Claims** section.

![additional-claims.png](https://cdn.us.document360.io/37f15d15-eeac-4caf-9724-25918cca6992/Images/Documentation/uuid-8c484c4f-fdd9-c327-ffb2-f748ec8f59ff(3).png)
8. The next step is to assign the role and organization to the user. Navigate back to the application and select the **User and groups** section from the left navigation bar. You can then see the list of users.
  1. To assign the **role**, check the checkbox against the user, and click on the **Edit assignment** button.

![edit-assignment-for-role.png](https://cdn.us.document360.io/37f15d15-eeac-4caf-9724-25918cca6992/Images/Documentation/uuid-4e0265de-b895-f2f0-b05b-3c6c5da401a0(3).png)

On the opened page, click on **Select a role** and assign the desired role from the list. Click **Select** on the bottom of the page and then click **Assign**. The role will be successfully configured for the user.

![role-assignment.png](https://cdn.us.document360.io/37f15d15-eeac-4caf-9724-25918cca6992/Images/Documentation/uuid-3ae30711-9821-ea5a-5078-6347ce6f9acc(3).png)
  2. To assign the **organization**, click on the user to assign the organization name to the relevant user. From the user details page, select **Edit properties**.

![edit-properties-org.png](https://cdn.us.document360.io/37f15d15-eeac-4caf-9724-25918cca6992/Images/Documentation/uuid-7518ab0c-8979-bf91-82ad-72b5cc0ba724(3).png)

Go to the **Job Information** tab, and add the organization name such as *Default Organization* against the Company Name. To assign the user to multiple organizations, separate the organization names with commas. Click **Save** from the bottom left of the page to save the settings.

![org-name-defined.png](https://cdn.us.document360.io/37f15d15-eeac-4caf-9724-25918cca6992/Images/Documentation/uuid-0d7708db-6eaa-4946-81e4-221fddf1d197(3).png)
9. The role and organization will be successfully assigned to the user.

### 4. Configure single sign-on in Securiti

1. In Securiti, on the **System Settings** menu choose **Organizational > Access Management > Single Sign-On**.

![](data:image/png;base64,)
2. In the **Single Sign-On** page, click **Configure Single Sign-On**.
3. On the **Single Sign-On Configuration** page under **Configuration Details** area, apply the following settings:

| Parameters | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Name | Enter a convenient name for the SSO configuration. |
| HTTP Binding | From the dropdown menu: - Choose **POST** to send SAML requests and responses using the HTTP POST binding. Securiti embeds the SAML message in an auto-submitting HTML form. - Choose **Redirect** to send SAML requests using the HTTP Redirect binding. Securiti embeds the SAML message in the URL query string. If your IdP requires a signed request with this binding, you must enable the **Allow signature** toggle below and select a signature algorithm. |
| Default User Role (only applied if JIT user provisioning is enabled) | Choose the role that Securiti assigns to new users who are signing in for the first time via Single Sign-On. |
| Default Organizations (only applied if JIT user provisioning and Organizations feature is enabled) | Use the tools to build a list of organizations to which Securiti assigns new users who are signing in for the first time via Single Sign-On. |
| Force SSO Login | Choose one of the following: - **All Users** to force all Securiti users and administrators log in via single-sign-on. - **Non Admin Users** to force all users except those with Administrator role to log in via single-sign-on. With this option, Securiti administrators can still log in using their local credentials. > [!NOTE] > **Note** > > If you encounter an issue with SSO-based access once you configure the All Users option, contact [support@securiti.ai](mailto:support@securiti.ai) for help. |
| SSO Enforced Domain(s) | Click the domains available below the input field to select the specific domains on which you want to enable SSO. This lets you force the users of selected domains to log in through SSO. These domains are available within your tenant. |
| Enable JIT User Provisioning | Mark the checkbox if you want to enable [just-in-time user provisioning](/latest/docs/configuring-single-sign-on-understanding-just-in-time-user-provisioning). |
| Provision SSO Users who log in through Self Service Portal | Mark this check to enable the users who are signing up via the Self Service Portal, become internal users with the role and organization you are assigning above. |
| Allow signature | For your HTTP Binding, enable this toggle if your IdP requires the signature, and choose the signature algorithm from the SigAlg menu. It supports both bindings: - POST binding - Redirect binding |
| Sign SAML Request | This checkbox appears only when you enable the **Allow signature** toggle. Select this option to force the SAML request to include the signature in the URL, even when you are using POST binding. Normally, POST binding places the signature inside the XML payload. This option lets you configure SSO with identity providers that require the signature to be included in the URL. |
| SigAlg | From the dropdown menu **SigAlg**, select a signature algorithm to sign the requests. |
| Source | Choose **XML FILE**, then click the link for Upload metadata XML file and choose the XML file you downloaded from ADFS earlier. |

![Configuration settings for Single Sign-On with various user options and links displayed.](https://cdn.us.document360.io/37f15d15-eeac-4caf-9724-25918cca6992/Images/Documentation/SSO_generic_configurations_page.png)

SSO_generic_configurations_page
4. Click **Test Single Sign-On**.

Securiti tests the configuration to make sure it is valid. If the tests succeed, proceed to the next step. Otherwise, double-check the Single Sign-On configuration settings.
5. Mark the checkbox for **Activate SSO upon saving the configuration** if you want to apply the SSO settings immediately.
6. Click **Save Configuration**.
7. If you want to test the SSO functionality immediately, restart your browser.
